editorial.headline: Technical Verification, Validation and the Evidence Behind Compliance
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 71203 covers objective technical assurance work, from carbon-footprint verification to industrial commissioning, with full national foreign ownership and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
Technical verification and validation is the business of establishing, through objective evidence, that a product, process or system meets its technical requirements and works for its intended purpose. It is a disciplined assurance activity: not merely an opinion on performance, but a formal confirmation built on evidence. Its remit also includes validation for intended future use or application, including projects involving greenhouse-gas environmental information and carbon economic value.

The verification side is equally broad. The activity can confirm that defined requirements have been met for organisations and projects in the greenhouse-gas information sector, emissions projects and reports, domestic-component levels, company-benefit weighting, financial-sector matters and carbon footprints. It also encompasses industrial-process commissioning, quality assurance and quality control. Taken together, this is an activity for businesses whose work sits where technical claims, performance requirements and documented evidence must be brought into alignment.

Businesses may register at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That is the straightforward national position in the record: a foreign investor may hold the full permitted stake in a company registered for this activity. The practical identity of the business, however, still needs to remain faithful to the assurance work described here—validation, verification, commissioning, quality assurance and quality control supported by objective evidence.

Bali does not alter that picture into a present registration ban. The province’s standing rule permanently blocks PMA registration, island-wide, for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. For this activity, however, the record states that OSS risk at the Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. Bali’s status is therefore recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: not a claim that every operational question disappears, but a clear indication that the provincial moratorium is not the barrier for this activity at the stated scale. For founders, the honest reading is uncomplicated: full foreign ownership is nationally available, and the Bali record does not mark this activity as blocked for PMA registration.
